touches.text: Tool: a complete primitive. Has users, not an owner. Lives in cairn/tools/. Its data for a holder lives under that holder: ~/.cairn/devices/<device>/<instance>/tools/<tool>/
Coding Ticket: what we usually mean.
Has its own workflow stamped on it (the state string, with the cursor).
The ticket owns its refusals: a gate refuses a crossing on the ticket's behalf (ruling 2026-08-10). The gates are housed in harbor_master.
Own foundational components (bus, ground loop, rack, shims, scheduler, launcher, harbor_master).

"it owns the gates only because we had to have some place to put them, but it does not control anything." The gates refuse on the ticket's behalf (ruling 2026-08-10: "the gate is the refuser but it's doing so on behalf of the ticket. so the ticket owns the refusal.")
TOOLS: base, artifact, charter, operator_inbox, proof_coverage, question, system_word; machine learning_block
VERBS: crossing, watch, clear. clear is the PROVED gate it houses on the ticket's behalf.
TESTER MACHINE, CodeMother's (was the tester device, cairn/devices/tester/)
Runs a proof as its own process and writes a validation record (claim, caller, date, method, verdict, evidence, falsifier, horizon).
gate: the == compare, in one place. A gate opens when every expected equals its actual. No oracle, ever.

The crossing is the ticket's own act. The gate's probe (the same kind that sends notice of gate passage) tells the passing ticket "you can now advance to X", and the ticket updates itself. (Q#61, Akien 2026-10-27)

open_questions.text: Test from the charters: "a thing that holds state is a machine, not a tool" (verdict machine, 2026-08). Is that still the line between 1.2.1 and 1.2.2, or is it "has glue / has several tools"?
Earlier (2026-08-06) sleep's trigger was idle, "3 hours without a human", not an hour of the day. Now it's a clock entry (2300). Is it the clock now, or both (at 2300, if no human for N hours)?
"Away windows" (you tell Cairn you'll be gone x to y) were ruled to the cairn device 2026-09-30. Are they entries on the same scheduled list? What does Cairn do differently while you're away?

What keeps the after-failure check from being a lock pick: a reader other than the builder (a cold cheap model, as rehearsal), the finding recording both whys verbatim and which lost, a pass that dies with its one ticket, a per-sieve count of passes that reds the sieve past some number? Which of these, or what else?
